title: Sequence-Length Cost Profile and Routing Recommendations (Hosted API)
content:
Purpose:
This working spreadsheet and notes explore how request sequence-length distributions drive per-token COGS, margin leakage, and the best routing/batching levers for the Hosted API. Goal is pragmatic routing rules + batching/window knobs that reduce marginal token cost by 10–30% for model families and regions with long-tail sequences, without increasing p99 latency above SLO.

Background / motivation:
- Most existing unit-econ work slices by model and region; we’ve under-indexed on sequence-length as a first-order cost driver.
- Observation from traces: a small fraction (~6–8%) of requests produce >2x of tokens vs median and contribute ~25% of total token consumption in some verticals (summaries, codegen).
- Long sequences reduce batching efficiency (fewer requests per batch for same token throughput) and inflate KV cache cold-miss penalty on decoder-heavy models.

Key assumptions (spreadsheet tab: assumptions):
- Per-GPU token throughput and hourly GPU cost per region are pulled from node-costs.csv (sheet tab: infra-costs).
- Per-model effective FLOP/token mapped to an execution latency curve (sheet tab: perf-curves).
- Batching policy: window-based (W ms) + max batch size (N). Current default W=20ms, N=64.
- L2 cache hit model for prefix caching: hit rate scales with repeated prompt patterns; assume base hit rate 12% for open-ended chat, 35% for instruction-following templates.
- Pricing: hosted API list price abstracted to per-token revenue across tiers; model selection affects revenue (higher quality models priced higher).

Data sources used:
- 30-day traffic trace (sampled) by request: model, region, sequence_length, tokens_out, tokens_in, latency, customer_tier. (sheet tab: traces-30d)
- Observed batch sizes and waiting windows from serving logs (sheet tab: batch-log-30d)
- Regional GPU price card as of 2024-01-01 (sheet tab: infra-costs)
- Recent model variant perf profiles (sheet tab: model-profiles)

Methodology (spreadsheet tab: calc-engine):
1) Bucket requests by sequence-length percentiles: short (<=32 tokens), medium (33–256), long (257–1024), xlong (>1024).
2) For each bucket, compute average tokens/request, mean batch efficiency (requests per batch vs ideal), and KV cache effective token-saved multiplier.
3) Convert throughput -> required GPU-seconds using model perf curves; multiply by regional GPU $/s to get marginal COGS per token for that bucket.
4) Simulate routing policies (local-region-only, cross-region-fallback, model-variant-fallback) and capture added network egress cost + latency delta.
5) Calculate contribution to total monthly tokens and margin impact per bucket.

Key findings (summary numbers pulled from sheet: summary):
- Median request token size: 48 tokens. Mean request token size: 230 tokens (skewed by tail).
- Buckets contribution to token volume: short 18%, medium 42%, long 30%, xlong 10%.
- Effective per-token COGS by bucket (global-weighted, v1 assumptions): short $0.000006, medium $0.000009, long $0.000018, xlong $0.000042.
- Long and xlong buckets are 2–7x more expensive per token than medium/short due to lower batching efficiency and KV re-computation.
- Routing to cheaper model-variant (quantized 4-bit, slightly lower perf) reduces marginal COGS for long/xlong by ~35% but increases model quality failure rate (as simulated) by 3–6% depending on task.

Scenario simulations (sheet tab: scenarios):
A) Base (current defaults): aggregate per-token margin = 62% (revenue minus COGS)/revenue; total monthly COGS = $1.12M.
B) Aggressive sequence-aware routing (route short->fast-smaller model; long->high-capacity pinned nodes with longer batching window; xlong->dedicated long-seq workers): projected COGS reduced to $0.83M (-26%), margin up to 69%.
C) Conservative (fallback-only when p95 latency > SLO): COGS -8%.
D) Cross-region spill into lower-cost region (adds avg 12ms RTT + $0.000002 egress per request): saves 9% COGS but increases p95 by ~9ms on average.

Sensitivity notes (sheet tab: sensitivity):
- Batching window tradeoff: increasing W from 20ms -> 35ms improves batch density for long sequences by 18% but increases median latency by ~4–6ms. For mixed workloads, window=28ms achieves a good operating point.
- Cache hit rate: a +10ppt improvement in prefix cache hit rate yields ~7% overall token savings for medium+long buckets. Workload-specific caching is high-leverage.
- Model throughput variance: if real-world perf worse by 15% vs perf curves, COGS gap widens disproportionately for xlong.

Operational routing recommendations (prioritized):
1) Sequence-length-aware model routing (P0): add a pre-routing step that inspects request request_length_bucket and assigns to model-variant+pool. Rules: short->small fast variant, medium->standard, long->high-throughput pool (pinned), xlong->dedicated long-seq machines with larger batch windows.
  - Rationale: cheap win; avoids overprovisioning high-capacity nodes for short requests.
  - Expected savings: 12–20% within 90 days.
2) Adaptive batching window per pool (P0): expose pool-level W config; default W_long=28ms, W_xlong=40ms. Instrument p50/p95 latency changes and set auto-rollback if p95 > SLO+10ms.
3) Prefix caching policy tuning (P1): raise heuristics for instruction-following templates, implement per-customer cache warmed hints. Estimate 5–10% token reduction for FAQ/chat verticals.
4) Model-variant fallback path (P1): when capacity constrained, route long requests to quantized variant with quality-aware guardrails (e.g., run a lightweight classifier that declines for tasks labeled as "high-fidelity").
5) Cross-region spill (P2): only for batchable, non-interactive requests where RTT impact < 15ms and cost delta > 8%.

Risk and quality guardrails:
- Quality regression: for quantized variants, require a small canary with A/B evals on prod prompt-set and an automatic rollback if quality delta > 4% on key metrics (ROUGE/BLEU or task-specific).
- Latency SLO violation: instrument synthetic traffic that mimics long sequences; use autoscaling target to ensure p95 headroom before widening windows.
- Billing surprises: track per-customer egress and cross-region cost separately in billing dashboard; add threshold alerts.

Estimated roadmap & owners (simple action table):
- Week 1–2: Add sequence-length bucket to API request logs and create aggregated daily rollups (owner: Samir).
- Week 2–4: Implement sequence-aware pre-routing and create a test pool for long-seq (owner: Miguel).
- Week 3–6: Expose pool W as config and test W_long/W_xlong variants on canary (owner: Lena).
- Week 4–8: Run canary for model-variant quantized routing and evaluate quality metrics; gating on quality delta < 4% (owner: Priya).
- Week 6–12: Production rollout and monitor cost dashboard baseline vs target (owner: product-optimize).

Open questions / TODO (working notes):
- Need better per-customer sequence-profile segmentation: currently use global buckets but customers vary widely (analytics tab: per-customer-buckets).
- How to express pricing differentiation if we route low-cost variants transparently? Legal/comms input needed.
- Investigate whether long-seq dedicated pools should be metered differently (dedicated pricing). Ops question: will customers accept higher latency in exchange for lower per-token price?

Appendix: spreadsheet tabs and important formulae (human readable):
- traces-30d: raw sample of requests (columns: ts, customer, model, region, tokens_in, tokens_out, seq_len)
- infra-costs: region, gpu_type, $/hour, vcpu, mem
- model-profiles: model_name, tokens_per_sec_at_seq=64, tokens_per_sec_at_seq=512, kv-memory-usage
- calc-engine: per-bucket COGS = sum_over_models((tokens/throughput_seconds) * gpu_$per_sec) / tokens
- scenarios: scenario_name, routing_matrix, expected_cogs, delta_margin, notes
- sensitivity: parameter sweep of W, cache_hit_rate, model_throughput_multiplier

Notes to self (choppy):
- need better name than 'xlong' but leaving for now; could use 'very_long' but keep consistent across sheets.
- include a small example row showing math: Example: model Zippy-2 large @ seq 1024 consumes 1.8 GPU-s per 1k tokens in region us-west (gpu_$s=0.0025) -> marginal COGS ~ $0.0045 per 1k tokens => $0.0000045 per token. bad calc? double-check perf curve mapping.

Immediate asks for data team:
- Provide 90-day traces (not sampled) aggregated by customer and seq_bucket. Ticket: ENGINF-1423.
- Validate perf curves for model Zippy-2 and Velo-7 (PR referenced above).

If we want to be conservative for launch, start with sequence-aware routing for short vs not-short. That gives quick operational savings with low risk and buys time to tune long-seq pools.

End of doc - this is a working draft, will iterate after canary data.
